title: Change affirmative olla into negative
summary: Keep the subject and context while changing only the polarity pattern.
objectives: Map each affirmative form to its negative pair.
Keep person agreement unchanged across the transformation.

sections.title: A six-person transformation map
paragraphs: To make an affirmative olla sentence negative, replace the finite olla form with the matching negative verb plus ole.
For example, olen becomes en ole and ovat becomes eivät ole. The person stays the same.

sections.title: Change one thing at a time
paragraphs: Read the source meaning and target meaning first. Keep the subject and supplied context unchanged.
Then choose the negative verb that matches the original subject and add ole.

examples.finnish: Minä olen täällä. → Minä en ole täällä.
examples.english: I am here. → I am not here.

examples.finnish: Hän on valmis. → Hän ei ole valmis.
examples.english: He or she is ready. → He or she is not ready.

examples.finnish: He ovat kotona. → He eivät ole kotona.
examples.english: They are at home. → They are not at home.

commonMistakes: Do not change the subject during the transformation.
Do not change the supplied location or state.
Do not put an affirmative olla form after the negative verb.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Change Hän on rauhallinen. “He or she is calm.” → ____ “He or she is not calm.” Keep the subject and context unchanged.
practiceExercises.explanation: Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

Correct. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Me emme ole rauhallinen.” does not fit this subject or construction. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Hän ei on rauhallinen.” does not fit this subject or construction. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

sentenceExplanation.translation: He or she is not calm.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject + person-marked negative verb + ole + context

parts.role: subject: the person or people described by the sentence
parts.formation: subject pronoun; no ending is added

parts.role: negative verb: carries the person agreement
parts.formation: hän takes the negative-verb form ei

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: olla uses the fixed form ole after the negative verb

parts.role: context: tells the location or state
parts.formation: supplied as a complete fixed expression; no change is required

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Change Me olemme kotona. “We are at home.” → ____ “We are not at home.” Keep the subject and context unchanged.
practiceExercises.explanation: Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

Correct. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Te ette ole kotona.” does not fit this subject or construction. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Me ei olemme kotona.” does not fit this subject or construction. Me changes from olemme to emme ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
